arxiv-2010-06090.title: A Model-free Approach for Testing Association
arxiv-2010-06090.creator: Saptarshi Chatterjee
arxiv-2010-06090.description: Abstract The question of association between outcome and feature is generally framed in the context of a model on functional and distributional forms. Our motivating application is that of identifying serum biomarkers of angiogenesis, energy metabolism, apoptosis, and inflammation, predictive of recurrence after lung resection in node-negative non-small cell lung cancer patients with tumor stage T2a or less.

arxiv-2106-12536.title: Hunting for the nature of the enigmatic narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxy PKS 2004-447
arxiv-2106-12536.creator: M. Berton, G. Peluso, P. Marziani, S. Komossa, L. Foschini, S. Ciroi, S. Chen, E. Congiu, L. C. Gallo, I. Björklund, L. Crepaldi, F. Di Mille, E. Järvelä, J. Kotilainen, A. Kreikenbohm, N. Morrell, P. Romano, E. Sani, G. Terreran, M. Tornikoski, S. Vercellone, A. Vietri
arxiv-2106-12536.description: Abstract Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) galaxies are a class of active galactic nuclei (AGN) that, in some cases, can harbor powerful relativistic jets. One of them, PKS 2004-447, shows γ \gamma -ray emission, and underwent its first recorded multifrequency flare in 2019.

arxiv-2309-00927.title: A practical guide to loss measurements using the Fourier transform of the transmission spectrum Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2309-00927.creator: Hannah Thiel, 1,* Bianca Nardi, 1 Alexander Schlager, 1 Stefan Frick, 1 and Gregor Weihs 1
arxiv-2309-00927.description: Abstract Analyzing the internal loss characteristics and multimodedness of (integrated) optical devices can prove difficult. One technique to recover this information is to Fourier transform the transmission spectrum of optical components. This article gives instruction on how to perform the transmission measurement, prepare the data, and interpret the Fourier spectrum.

arxiv-2310-16584.title: Learning to Explain: A Model-Agnostic Framework for Explaining Black Box Models
arxiv-2310-16584.creator: Oren Barkan Yuval Asher Amit Eshel Yehonatan Elisha Noam Koenigstein, The Open University Tel Aviv University
arxiv-2310-16584.description: Abstract We present Learning to Explain (LTX), a model-agnostic framework designed for providing post-hoc explanations for vision models. The LTX framework introduces an “explainer” model that generates explanation maps, highlighting the crucial regions that justify the predictions made by the model being explained. To train the explainer, we employ a two-stage process consisting of initial pretraining followed by per-instance finetuning.

arxiv-2402-00185.title: Energetic particle activity in AD Leo: Detection of a solar-like type-IV burst
arxiv-2402-00185.creator: Atul Mohan, Surajit Mondal, Sven Wedemeyer, Natchimuthuk Gopalswamy
arxiv-2402-00185.description: Abstract Context. AD Leo is a young and active M dwarf with high flaring rates across the X-ray-to-radio bands. Flares accelerate particles in the outer coronal layers and often impact exo-space weather. Wide-band radio dynamic spectra let us explore the evolution of particle acceleration activity across the corona.

Nikbakht are with Centre Tecnològic de Telecomunicacions de Catalunya (CTTC), Spain. G. Geraci is with Telefónica and UPF, Spain. S. Kang and S. Rangan are with NYU Wireless, USA. A. Lozano is with

arxiv-2402-03517.description: Abstract This article proposes a generative neural network architecture for spatially consistent air-to-ground channel modeling. The approach considers the trajectories of uncrewed aerial vehicles along typical urban paths, capturing spatial dependencies within received signal strength (RSS) sequences from multiple cellular base stations (gNBs).

arxiv-2408-04671.title: Prompt and Prejudice
arxiv-2408-04671.creator: Lorenzo Berlincioni, Luca Cultrera, Federico Becattini, Marco Bertini, Alberto Del Bimbo
arxiv-2408-04671.description: Abstract This paper investigates the impact of using first names in Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs), particularly when prompted with ethical decision-making tasks. We propose an approach that appends first names to ethically annotated text scenarios to reveal demographic biases in model outputs.

arxiv-2408-05179.title: Galactic Gas Models Strongly Affect the Determination of the Diffusive Halo Height
arxiv-2408-05179.creator: Pedro De La Torre Luque, Tim Linden
arxiv-2408-05179.description: Abstract The height of the Milky Way diffusion halo, above which cosmic-rays can freely escape the galaxy, is among the most critical, yet poorly known, parameters in cosmic-ray physics. Measurements of radioactive secondaries, such as 10 Be or 26 Al, which decay equivalently throughout the diffusive volume, are expected to provide the strongest constraints.

arxiv-2501-08280.title: Using Gamified Experiments to Tame Complexity: the case of the Schelling Model of Segregation
arxiv-2501-08280.creator: Aleix Nicolás Olivé, Luce Prignano, Dimitri Marinelli, Emanuele Cozzo
arxiv-2501-08280.description: Abstract Abstract: This study employs gamified experiments to investigate and refine the Schelling Model of Segregation, a framework that demonstrates how individual preferences can lead to systemic segregation. Using a movement selection algorithm derived from a board game adaptation of the classical Schelling Model, the research examines player strategies aimed at minimizing segregation and maximizing happiness within a controlled environment.

arxiv-2510-06468.title: BATTLE for Bitcoin: Capital-Efficient Optimistic Bridges with Large Committees
arxiv-2510-06468.creator: Sergio Demian Lerner, Ariel Futoransky
arxiv-2510-06468.description: Abstract We present BATTLE for Bitcoin , a DoS-resilient dispute layer that secures optimistic bridges between Bitcoin and rollups or sidechains. Our design adapts the BATTLE tournament protocol to Bitcoin’s UTXO model using BitVM-style FLEX components and garbled circuits with on-demand L1 security bonds.

pmc-13281651.title: How team forgiveness climate influences innovative performance in college student innovation teams: a moderated mediation model
pmc-13281651.creator: Honghao Hu, Chao Li, Jonas Valkonen, Haoluan Fu
pmc-13281651.description: By integrating team design theory and organizational learning theory within an input–process–output (IPO) framework, this study examines the relationships among team forgiveness climate, team learning from mistakes and team innovative performance.
